subject: Post-demo: Orion Health comparative eval & next tests
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Kate Miller <kate@orionhealth.ai>, Evan Zhou <evan.zhou@orionhealth.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-14T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: Orion Health comparative eval & next tests

Hi Kate / Evan —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we can align on a short comparative evaluation that focuses on model quality (hallucination, factuality), latency at target payloads, and error/regression checks against your current in-house inference.

Attachments I dropped into the Drive link and attached here: orion-eval-promptset-v1.csv (seed prompts + customer-sensitive subset), redwood-vs-hyperscaler-matrix-20280814.xlsx (matrix of test axes + suggested configurations), and a short hallucination-checklist.md we use for automated probes.

Immediate asks / next tests (proposed):
- Run the seed prompt set across these endpoints: Redwood-hosted standard-1 (fp16), Redwood-optimized-quant (int8), HyperscalerA-endpoint (default), HyperscalerB-endpoint (quant if available).
- Metrics to capture per-prompt: hallucination_rate (binary scorer + human spot-check on 5%), factuality_score (fact-checker F1), max/median token-latency at 95th percentile, and output token counts.
- Regression checks: run the last production prompt sample (we included a 200-prompt regression subset) and compare unchanged-answer rate and drop-in user-visible changes.
- Failure modes to log: hallucinated citations, truncated completions, and inconsistent entity normalization.

Internal owners — please see assignments below and confirm on Monday:
- Ben: run the cross-endpoint runs and produce the raw CSVs (include request/response, timing, model config). Use a 50-shot parallelism profile to reflect Orion's expected concurrency.
- Lauren: expand the promptset with 20 targeted patient-care prompts from the attached sensitive subset and tag for hallucination-priority; prepare evaluation rubric and the human spot-check instructions.
- Sergio: coordinate a follow-up call with Kate/Evan next week to review preliminary numbers and decide whether to scope a full POC.

Kate/Evan — would Tuesday 8/16 at 11am PT work for a 30-min sync? We can walk a short results table and propose a plan for a 4-week POC if the numbers look interesting.

Thanks — I’ll kick off the runs internally today and share a preliminary CSV by Monday EOD PT.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments: orion-eval-promptset-v1.csv (CSV), redwood-vs-hyperscaler-matrix-20280814.xlsx (Excel), hallucination-checklist.md (text)
From: Kate Miller <kate@orionhealth.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Evan Zhou <evan.zhou@orionhealth.ai>
Date: 2028-08-14T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Orion Health comparative eval & next tests

Thanks Marissa — great summary. Tuesday 8/16 11am PT works for us.

Couple of notes from our side:
- We can run the HyperscalerA endpoint and share raw outputs; HyperscalerB requires an internal request to opt-in for quantized models — we can try to get that by Monday but can’t promise.
- Security wants to see the minimal data flow diagram and confirmation that PII will be hashed before leaving our environment; Evan, can you add the security contact in a follow-up?
- For the human spot-checks, we prefer 10% sampling on the sensitive subset (we have stricter tolerance there).

I’ll upload a zipped version of our regression sample tomorrow if that helps.

—Kate
Director, AI Engineering
Orion Health

Got it — I’ll spin up the benchmark runs first thing Monday and will standardize output to the CSV schema in the Drive link. A few clarifying Qs:
1) For HyperscalerA/B runs we should capture the full response headers (model id, config) — confirm yes?
2) Do we want to normalize tokenization differences before computing hallucination rate, or compute on raw outputs and flag tokenization divergences separately?

Plan: start with raw outputs and include a tokenization-mapping column so analysts can choose normalization after. I’ll include timing at request, first-byte, and last-byte.

Thanks — I’ll take the sensitive subset and add the 20 patient-care prompts. A couple of editorial points for the rubric: 
- Hallucination definition: any generated assertion about a patient that cannot be traced to the prompt or a linked factual source.
- Severity buckets: Minor (formatting/terminology), Major (incorrect clinical assertion), Critical (erroneous medical advice).

I’ll prepare the human spot-check instructions and a small lookup table for the QA reviewers so the 10% sample requested by Kate is easy to audit. Expected deliverable: expanded promptset CSV + rubric doc by Monday EOD.

Lauren
Product Manager, Evaluations | Redwood Inference
